1 · Upload your Excel mastersheet

One row per patient, one column per variable. Repeated measures go in separate columns with the timepoint in the name (e.g. VAS_baseline, VAS_W1). Your data never leaves this computer.

Drop your Excel file here or click to browse
.xlsx, .xls or .csv

Data

Columns
Click a cell to change it · rename a column in its heading · ◀ ▶ move · ⇅ sort · ✕ delete · ↑ ↓ move rows

Report details

Pick a template, then check the version. Name the software actually used for the analysis you report.

Or try an example dataset

Simulated studies that show the expected sheet layout and the analyses. Open one to explore the app, or download it as Excel to see how to arrange your own data.

2 · Groups

Choose the column that defines the study groups, or analyse all patients as one group. Labels are used in tables, figures and comments.

One group: tables describe all patients; repeated measures are compared over time within the same patients (paired t-test / Wilcoxon, repeated-measures ANOVA / Friedman).

Use ↑/↓ to set the column order of groups in tables.

Variables

Detected automatically — check and adjust. Repeated measures (same name, different timepoints) are analysed as one outcome with one table. Single variables sharing the same Table name appear together in one table.

All variables: Distribution of all numeric:

Distribution: Auto uses the normality test chosen in step 3 (Shapiro-Wilk by default) in every group — a single variable is non-parametric if any group fails; a repeated outcome if more than 25% of group × timepoint cells fail. The chip shows the result. Levels: order of categories, comma-separated (the first is used for relative risk / odds ratio).

Calculated variables

Create a new column from existing ones, e.g. BMI from weight and height, a change score, a total score or BMI classes. The column is added to the sheet (undo with ↶ in step 1) and to the variables above.

Repeated measures

Detected from column names with timepoints (e.g. VAS_baseline, VAS_W1). Create your own from any numeric columns, edit which columns enter and their timepoint labels and order, or ungroup a measure back into single variables. In the table above you can also untick single timepoints or analyse a measure as separate variables.

3 · Timepoints

Each repeated outcome has its own timepoints: tick which enter, rename them and set their order for that outcome only. Labels you type here are used in its table, comments and figure.

Shared timepoint names

Default names for the timepoint tokens found in column names. Outcomes use these unless you renamed a timepoint above. Unticking a token here leaves it out of every outcome.

4 · Statistical tests

Repeated measures

How outcomes measured several times in the same patients are tested. Change within each group needs Change over time within each group ticked above (one-group studies always test it).

Legend

Figures by variable & live preview

Choose the chart type of each variable and, if you like, its own caption. The preview redraws as you change any figure option on this page.

8 · Advanced analyses

Optional. Each analysis adds its own table (and ROC figure) after the main results. Categorical predictors are compared with their first level (group order / levels order from step 2). Patients with missing values are left out of that analysis.

9 · Flowchart

Appearance — colours, corners, lines, text

Section labels

Leave a label empty to use the standard text shown in it.

10 · Results by variable

Every result for each variable and repeated measure: descriptive statistics with normality per group, every candidate test with its statistic, P value and effect size (✓ marks the test used in the report), pairwise comparisons, change over time and mixed ANOVA. For checking your data — the report uses only the tests chosen in step 4. Open Data of each group under a variable to see every patient's value (outliers in orange, missing in red); click a value to change it and the results update at once. Changes go into the sheet and the report too (↶ Undo to go back).

⚙ Options — filter, tables, statistics, figure, outliers

11 · Report

Review everything below. You can edit the text boxes — your edits go into the Word file. The format changes only this report; your settings in steps 4–9 stay as they are.
